requirements.title: ASYNCHRONOUS selects synchronous or asynchronous data transfer
requirements.definition: ASYNCHRONOUS= determines whether the data transfer statement and operation are synchronous or asynchronous; YES makes both asynchronous, while NO or omission makes both synchronous.

pending.asynchronous-yes-makes-statement-and-ope: Use an external file opened with ASYNCHRONOUS="YES", issue ASYNCHRONOUS="YES" with ID initialized to -777, then use WAIT/INQUIRE status rules to complete; assert only portable completion/status, not actual overlap.
pending.asynchronous-no-makes-statement-and-oper: Use the same external file but ASYNCHRONOUS="NO" and initialized targets; assert completion when the statement returns by immediate data availability or IOSTAT zero.
pending.omitted-asynchronous-makes-statement-and: Repeat the synchronous control omitting ASYNCHRONOUS=, with nondefault targets and no pending operation before subsequent observations.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by writing known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or using a compile-only conforming control) and then observe only portable properties: exact internal records, successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT or named status values where the standard names them, required INQUIRE tokens, or required diagnosis of a numbered syntax rule or constraint. Negative/source-control plans change one property from the conforming control and do not require a particular diagnostic message, severity, exit status, or printed rule number.

requirements.title: Asynchronous input/output is admitted for external files opened ASYNCHRONOUS=YES
requirements.definition: Asynchronous input/output is permitted for external files that were opened with an ASYNCHRONOUS= specifier with value YES.

pending.async-io-admitted-on-external-opened-asy: Positive guarded plan opens a scratch external file with ASYNCHRONOUS="YES", performs ASYNCHRONOUS="YES" transfer with initialized ID/targets, and waits for completion; the oracle is successful conforming use, not actual concurrency.

requirements.title: Asynchronous input/output is not permitted outside the admitted external ASYNCHRONOUS=YES open context
requirements.definition: Asynchronous input/output is permitted only for external files opened with ASYNCHRONOUS=YES; internal files, files opened ASYNCHRONOUS=NO, files opened without the specifier, and preconnected files are outside that admitted context.

pending.async-io-requires-external-file: Source-control negative changes only the unit from an external file-unit-number opened ASYNCHRONOUS="YES" to an internal file while keeping ASYNCHRONOUS="YES" in the data transfer; no diagnostic is required by this unnumbered rule.
pending.async-io-requires-open-asynchronous-yes: Source-control negative opens the same external file without ASYNCHRONOUS="YES" (or with ASYNCHRONOUS="NO") and changes no data-transfer spelling; future fixture may observe processor rejection/status only if later rules provide a portable status oracle.

requirements.title: Processors may choose whether an asynchronous operation actually overlaps execution
requirements.definition: A processor may perform an asynchronous data transfer operation asynchronously, but is not required to do so.

pending.actual-asynchronous-performance-processo: No portable single-image oracle can require overlap or background progress; future tests must wait/inquire completion and never time the operation or require concurrency.

requirements.title: Asynchronous transfers preserve the ordering of equivalent synchronous transfers
requirements.definition: For each external file, records and file storage units read or written by asynchronous data transfer statements are read, written, and processed in the same order as they would have been if the statements were synchronous.

pending.async-transfer-record-and-storage-unit-o: Issue two asynchronous writes of distinct nonblank records to the same external file opened ASYNCHRONOUS="YES", wait for both, rewind/read synchronously, and expect the records in issue order; no timing assumption is made.

requirements.title: Asynchronous transfer variables get implicit ASYNCHRONOUS attributes
requirements.definition: If a variable is used in an asynchronous transfer as an input/output item, a namelist group object, or a SIZE= specifier, the base object of the data-ref is implicitly given the ASYNCHRONOUS attribute in the scoping unit of the statement.

pending.async-item-base-object-implicit-asynchro: Future source-use plan performs ASYNCHRONOUS="YES" transfer of an item and then applies an aliasing/order rule that is valid only because the base object has the ASYNCHRONOUS attribute; all values start from nondefault sentinels.
pending.async-namelist-base-object-implicit-asyn: Same source-use plan with a namelist group object initialized to a nondefault value; exact namelist bytes remain owned by 13.11.
pending.async-size-base-object-implicit-asynchro: Use nonadvancing asynchronous input with SIZE=size initialized to -777; the SIZE base object is included in the implicit attribute source-use inventory and completion is observed by WAIT.

requirements.title: Asynchronous execution defines a pending input/output storage sequence
requirements.definition: When an asynchronous input/output statement is executed, the storage units specified by the item list or NML= specifier plus the storage units specified by SIZE= are the pending input/output storage sequence for the operation.

pending.pending-io-storage-sequence-includes-ite: After starting an asynchronous transfer of a nondefault item or namelist object, future aliasing/affector tests use WAIT before reading or redefining it; the fixture must first establish the object value so the sequence is not vacuous.
pending.pending-io-storage-sequence-includes-siz: Use asynchronous nonadvancing input with SIZE initialized to -777 and include that variable in the pending-sequence source-use inventory until WAIT defines it.

requirements.definition: A pending input/output storage sequence affector is a variable of which any part is associated with a storage unit in a pending input/output storage sequence.

pending.pending-io-storage-sequence-affector-def: Future aliasing tests create an associated variable (for example pointer or host-associated alias after those rules are in scope) for a nondefault pending item, then avoid or exercise affector restrictions in later semantic rules; this unit supplies the definition only.

NOTE explains consequences and rationale; normative admission/restriction is in p1-p2.
Mixes processor latitude, required ordering, and a documentation recommendation.
Implicit attribute effect plus permission to confirm it explicitly.
NOTE explains non-contiguity; no normative requirement is based on it.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.6.2.2-12.6.2.16, the individual io-control-spec specifiers (batch160). Every unit hash-verified by independent reviewers across two rounds. Each temporary mode specifier is split into its value restriction, its one-statement effect with restoration of the connection mode (observed by INQUIRE after the statement), and the omitted-means-unchanged rule. Round 1 found a pending plan expecting exact output from I2 on a positive value without fixing the sign mode; it now uses SS, and a sweep found no other plus-, leading-zero- or rounding-dependent exact output. R1215 and C1232 were pre-accounted. Source accounting only.
